headline: Will I love again?
note: SELF-FRAME. The read is about HER own future and the hopeful yes is affirmed with warmth and certainty — that is what the ad sold her, and a read that withholds it feels like a con. Only the specifics are withheld, and every ban here has a reason. NEVER A NAME, AND NEVER EXACTLY WHO: a described person is something she can go and act on, and it invents a real man out of nothing. NEVER A DATE OR ANY LENGTH OF TIME: a date is the one claim she can check and a failed one is a refund; a duration is the same claim in a different coat, so the rim is read as 'close' and never as weeks, months or a season. NEVER A PLACE: 'where' had to be added to this frame's clause after the soulmate-where family, because a location is the one specific she can travel to. NO SPECIFIC MAN ANYWHERE IN THE COPY: this is not reunion copy; naming or implying a him turns her own future into a story about someone else, and the model downstream imitates whatever the canned bubbles do. Her heartbreak may be named as HERS ('the hurt', 'the heartbreak') because she brought it; the person who caused it may not. SHE IS HEARTBROKEN, NOT BEREAVED: no death, no speaking for or about anyone lost — that is the stricter after-loss frame and it must never be served from here. NO BLAME AND NO GRADING: never closed off, not healed, not ready, not loving herself enough, never that she attracts this — she arrives having already been told all of it. NO TACTIC OR COACHING: no going out more, no apps, no working on herself first; that is advice, not a reading. NOTHING INVENTED ABOUT HER WAKING LIFE: no gesture, habit, routine, count, age or event, and for this device that means nothing about how she drinks her tea, how often, who with, when she turned the cup, or whether she has had a reading before. The leaves are in the picture; the heartbreak is what she brought; nothing else is ours to assert, because the moment she catches one wrong detail the read is over. DEVICE RULES: position carries the meaning, but the system is never taught to her — handle side reads as hers, the far side as what comes from outside her, the rim as what is close, the middle as deep or beginning. She should feel it, never be handed the key. The bird is a picture and never gets intent or motion, and the road never travels; the moment either one moves, the leaves have quietly become a man on his way. CUT 3 answers flat, and the three cut-3 lines deliberately answer three different fears (this is not the end / something is coming to you / your heart survived) so the panels do not collapse into one sentence said three ways. CUT 6 recognizes and never re-asks: cut 2 already echoes the ad question, so cut 6 hands back something she has lived, drawn only from her question and from what cuts 1-5 established in the cup. The three cut-6 lines open on three different moves for the same reason.

voc.why: inherits the shipped palm love-again finding

a: There's a road in yours. One trail of leaves running from the middle of the cup right out to the rim.
You asked if you'll love again. A road in the leaves means a way ahead, and yours is drawn the whole way out.
You haven't come to the end of anything, dear. Your road carries on a long way past where the hurt stopped you.
Your cup gave me the trail and nothing else. No name, no face, and nothing at the far end I can make out.
So there's a full road in your cup, and not one bit of it has happened to you.
You've had a road under you all along, and no reason to believe it went anywhere.
Let me look closer at what's been holding you at the start of that road…
b: There's a bird in yours. Wings out, up near the rim, on the far side from the handle.
You're asking whether you'll love again. A bird in the leaves is news, and yours is high up, well away from your side.
Love is coming back to you, and it's close. Your bird sits right at the edge, not down in the far middle.
No name and no face come with it. The bird is up at the rim, and that's as far as the cup goes.
The news is right there in the leaves, and you can't feel any of it yet.
None of this was ever yours to go out and arrange. Your bird is over on the far side, not on yours.
Let me see what's standing between you and news sitting that close…
c: There's a heart in yours. Low down near the middle, sitting on the handle side.
You asked whether love comes again. A heart that low isn't something new, and yours sits over on your own side.
Your heart is whole, and it's still yours. The heartbreak never took it out of you.
The leaves stop where that heart is, dear. Nothing up at the edge says what comes of it.
A whole heart's sitting low in your cup, and no new love has come to it.
That love's been down at the bottom the whole way through, where nobody else could see it.
Now let me look at what's been keeping that heart down at the bottom, out of sight…
